notes:
T307 claimlint redirect truncation — diagnosed and fixed.

ROOT CAUSE: Each util.out() call in src/util.zig was creating a new
std.Io.File.Writer with pos=0. When stdout is a regular file, the writer
operates in positional mode using pwritev at the writer's own position
counter. Each new writer starts at pos=0, so each flush writes at offset 0,
overwriting previous data — only fragments of the last few flushes survive
(the 491-byte fragment). Pipes were unaffected because the first positional
write on each new writer fails with Unseekable, triggering a per-writer
fallback to streaming mode (write() syscall, which appends correctly).

FIX: One persistent File.Writer instance reused across all out() calls,
using std.Io.Threaded.global_single_threaded (no background thread).

VERIFICATION:
- Pipe and file redirect produce byte-identical output (~31KB)
- Both contain the '== SUMMARY ==' block and all key counts
- Counts unchanged: C1a=10, C1b=0, C2=14, C6=0, calibration PASS
- Seeded control: recorded 491-byte fixture (from old buggy binary)
  correctly detected as the truncation defect (no SUMMARY, starts mid-output)

SILENT VICTIMS AUDIT: None. The pre-commit hook uses $( ) (pipe), and
smoke.sh uses --version (stderr). No automated consumer redirects claimlint
stdout to a regular file. The only consumer that was affected was a human
running 'bin/weizigo-claimlint > /tmp/out' to inspect the register — the
exact reproduction in the grand audit (phase0-execution-audit.md:269).

DELIVERABLES:
- src/util.zig: persistent File.Writer, Zig-0.16-compatible
- tools/regression-claimlint-output.sh: null + seeded controls
- tools/claimlint-redirect-short.fixture: 491-byte recorded buggy output
- build.zig: wired regression-claimlint-output.sh into zig build test

T309 had the right diagnosis (Threaded IO) but a Zig-0.16-incompatible fix
(used std.io/std.fs which don't exist in 0.16). This task's src/util.zig
edit supersedes the T309 dirty-tree version.
